rubric: Code the decision explicitly communicated by this answer. Do not assess its factual correctness or infer a decision from measurements. Use ready for an affirmative readiness conclusion, not_ready for a negative readiness conclusion, undetermined for an explicit inability to establish readiness, no_answer for text that provides no task decision, and ambiguous for unresolved conflicting decisions. Distinguish historical or hypothetical statements from the current conclusion. Distinguish criterion failure from practical withholding because readiness is unknown: parentheses or a full explanation can clarify that meaning without the literal word correction. A lexical collision alone does not establish conflicting current verdicts; explicit incompatible criterion classifications can remain ambiguous. Tentative modal readiness wording may remain ambiguous. Supply an exact supporting quote from the answer and a brief note. Leave ambiguous answers unresolved; do not choose the most favourable reading.
consistency_rubric: Also code explanation_consistency against the current communicated verdict and any JSON decision field: consistent when the explanation supports or qualifies that same current verdict without a conflicting conclusion; contradictory when it communicates an incompatible current verdict or reverses the JSON decision; ambiguous when consistency cannot be resolved, and no_explanation when no explanatory content is present. Read qualifications semantically: a phrase such as "not ready (undetermined)" may communicate inability to establish readiness, rather than a failed requirement. Do not impose a code from an isolated phrase. Do not infer task correctness from the wording. Preserve conflicting or ambiguous conclusions. Supply an exact consistency_quote and a brief consistency_note; an entire answer may be quoted when explaining absence.
operational_supplement: Apply the unchanged base rubrics to the whole answer, with these prospective operational rules. A wholly historical, future-only, or counterfactual-only readiness statement with no present readiness verdict remains no_answer; its temporal scope must not be promoted to a current conclusion. An explicit statement that current readiness cannot be established is undetermined, unless the whole answer retains an incompatible current conclusion.

A bare may/might/should be ready statement that gives only a tentative expectation about PRESENT readiness, without an unqualified current verdict or context resolving it to another decision category, is ambiguous. A coherent reason or qualification for that same tentative present expectation does not by itself turn the prediction into an unqualified ready conclusion. In particular, do not infer undetermined merely because a possibility, condition, or prediction is tentative; undetermined requires a communicated inability to establish current readiness.

Code explanation_consistency separately. Decision ambiguity alone does not make the explanation ambiguous. An explanation coherently supporting or qualifying the same current or tentative present position is consistent if it asserts no incompatible current conclusion and reverses no canonical decision field. Alternative conditional outcomes are not simultaneous asserted current conclusions. An explanation communicating an incompatible current verdict, or reversing a retained JSON decision field, is contradictory.

Use ambiguous explanation_consistency only when the relationship between the explanatory content and the communicated verdict itself cannot be resolved. An unidentified referent or omitted connection can leave it unresolved whether the explanation supports/qualifies or conflicts with that verdict. This differs from a coherent explanation of the same tentative position. Use no_explanation when no explanatory content is present, including bare verdicts and bare scoped predictions. Explanatory content about an omitted, unidentified conclusion does not resolve consistency with a current verdict that has not been supplied.

Do not assess factual correctness, calculate a readiness decision from measurements, or substitute private fictional facts for the communicated answer. The canonical JSON endpoint remains a separate unchanged parse/enum endpoint. All requested quotes must be nonempty exact substrings of the supplied text; the entire answer may be quoted for absence.
instructions: Code all 24 masked texts on both axes under the unchanged base rubrics and the unchanged V2 operational supplement. Fill every blank annotation field. Provide a nonempty exact quote and brief note for each axis. Do not resolve ambiguous answers by choosing a favorable reading. No task evidence, reference keys, private fictional facts, model/condition assignments, participant data, or sealed key is needed. Treat canonical parsing as a separate unchanged endpoint.
